leaves.scope_statement: The maximal globally hyperbolic development of generic asymptotically flat vacuum initial data (4-dimensional Einstein vacuum equations, Lambda = 0) has future null infinity I+ that is complete, and no future-incomplete causal geodesic is visible from I+. The class asserts hiddenness of singularities, not their absence.
leaves.quantifiers.formal: forall r in D0: exists G_r subset X^r_vac(AF) with G_r comeager: forall (Sigma,h,K) in G_r, letting (M,g) be the maximal globally hyperbolic development: exists a conformal completion (Mtilde,gtilde,Omega) of (M,g) at I+ such that (i) I+ is null with I+ diffeomorphic to R x S^2, and (ii) every null geodesic generator of I+ is future-complete, and forall future-inextendible causal geodesics gamma of (M,g) with finite affine length: not exists q in I+ and t0 in [0,T) with gamma([t0,T)) subset J^-(q) intersect M.
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D0.definition: admissible regularity indices, a tagged disjoint union: r = smooth (the smooth-with-decay default) or r = (sobolev,s,delta) with s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1). X^r_vac(AF) is the corresponding one-ended AF vacuum constraint manifold (Frechet for r = smooth; weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1} for r = (sobolev,s,delta)). The index r ranges over exactly D0, so the smooth branch is no longer typed as a pair and the class does not range over 'suitable' regularity. [rev12 F-2 well-typedness repair: F1-review-19 F-2, F2b-review-034 HF-034-1]
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D1.definition: comeager (residual) subsets of X^r_vac(AF): G_r = intersection over n >= 1 of U_n with each U_n open and dense in the named topology; equivalently X^r_vac(AF) minus G_r is meager
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D2.definition: one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data satisfying both constraint equations in the declared regularity class
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D3.definition: conformal completions of the maximal development at future null infinity: Omega > 0 on M, Omega = 0 and dOmega != 0 on I+, gtilde = Omega^2 g extends as a C^k Lorentzian metric to M union I+, I+ null and diffeomorphic to R x S^2
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D4.definition: future-directed causal geodesics gamma: [0,T) -> M that are future-inextendible in M, with T < infinity in affine parameter (unit speed in the timelike case). Qualifier aligned with visibility.definition and non_vacuity: future-inextendibility is what makes the terminal end a singularity. [R1 minor]
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D5.definition: pairs (q,t0) with q a point of I+ and t0 in [0,T) such that the tail gamma([t0,T)) is contained in the causal past J^-(q) intersected with M. leaves.genericity.ambient_space: the constraint manifold X^r_vac(AF) of one-ended asymptotically flat VACUUM initial data in the declared regularity class, carrying the topology induced from the weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1}. R1 F04 accepted: the topology is the SUBSPACE topology on the constraint set, not the topology of the unconstrained product (under the latter reading X_vac itself is meager and no G exists). X_vac is a closed subset of a Banach space, hence a Baire space, so comeagerness is non-vacuous and G is non-empty.
leaves.genericity.topology_or_measure: subspace topology induced on X^r_vac(AF); Frechet topology for the smooth-with-decay class. Gauge invariance is handled by noting every predicate here is diffeomorphism invariant; the quotient by asymptotically-identity diffeomorphisms is NOT used to define comeagerness and remains an open technical gap (see unresolved_items).
leaves.genericity.generic_set: G = intersection over n >= 1 of U_n with each U_n open and dense in X^r_vac(AF); equivalently the complement is meager (first category); G_r is non-empty because X_vac is Baire
leaves.genericity.excluded_set: the excluded set is REQUIRED to be meager; whether the named candidate families are meager is UNRESOLVED, so they are listed as obligations rather than as constructions. Candidates: data with a nonzero Killing field, data in the exactly-extendible (Cauchy-horizon) family, self-similar or scale-invariant data, finite-dimensional analytic families generated by continuation, and exactly symmetric data (see axis_registry and membership_ruling).
leaves.genericity.membership_ruling: set-level only: the class quantifies over a comeager set G of data; the schema does not decide membership of an individual datum. A single symmetric/stationary datum is expected outside G in the vacuum class, but that expectation is a proof obligation, not a schema field (flash-04 AMB-07 ruling).
leaves.genericity.class_change_warning: genericity is part of the class identity. The comeager form is this class. 'For all data' is strictly stronger. The dense-open form is ALSO strictly stronger, because a dense open set is comeager (it is the countable intersection of the constant family). The comeager form does not imply the dense-open form (a comeager set can have empty interior). No strengthening may be substituted silently. See genericity.transfer_failures for the two directions.
leaves.genericity.acceptance_alignment: Astra F1 acceptance names 'open dense'. This schema's frozen default is the residual/comeager form; open_dense_escape is registered below as a distinct STRICTLY STRONGER variant (a dense open set is comeager, so it implies the default) and is never silently substituted. A gate matching only the literal words 'open dense' would accept a stronger class than this one - recorded as a vocabulary risk.

leaves.genericity.transfer_failures[1].witness: let C be the comeager null set of the row above; then X minus C is meager and has full measure, so full measure does not yield comeagerness. (The irrationals are BOTH comeager and full-measure and therefore witness nothing - R1 F03.)
leaves.genericity.transfer_failures[2].witness: the irrationals are comeager with empty interior: a comeager set need not contain any nonempty open subset, so the comeager form does not yield a dense-open form
leaves.genericity.transfer_failures[3].witness: a fat Cantor set is nowhere dense (meager) yet has positive measure, so it is not contained in any countable union of finite-codimension submanifolds, which is null
leaves.genericity.transfer_holds[0].witness: a dense open set U is the countable intersection of the constant family {U}, hence comeager; the dense-open form implies the comeager form
leaves.genericity.transfer_holds[1].witness: a proper closed finite-codimension submanifold is closed and nowhere dense, so a countable union of them is meager; if the exceptional set is so covered, the property holds on a comeager set
leaves.genericity.variants[1].relation: implied by residual_comeager in a Baire space (a comeager set is dense); a dense set need not be comeager, so it is strictly weaker than the class default. [R2-16 corrected: was off-vocabulary and mislabelled incomparable]

leaves.visibility.singularity_definition: an incomplete causal geodesic: future-directed, future-inextendible in M, with finite affine length (unit speed in the timelike case). Curvature blow-up is NOT used as the definition of a singular point.
leaves.visibility.definition: a future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma: [0,T) -> M with T < infinity in affine parameter is visible from I+ iff there exists q in I+ AND t0 in [0,T) such that the TAIL gamma([t0,T)) is contained in J^-(q) intersect M. Visibility is a property of the singular END of the geodesic, so the tail formulation is used; requiring the whole geodesic to lie in J^-(q) would misclassify a geodesic that starts in the exterior and ends inside the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted]
leaves.visibility.visible_singularity_exists: exists gamma visible from I+ in the sense above
leaves.visibility.negation_conclusion: there is NO visible_singularity_from_I_plus: for every future-inextendible causal geodesic gamma of finite affine length, for every q in I+ and every t0 in [0,T), the tail gamma([t0,T)) is NOT contained in J^-(q) intersect M - no single point of I+ causally precedes the singular end of gamma. This is NOT equivalent to 'gamma is contained in B = M minus J^-(I+)': B-containment is strictly stronger, and a geodesic may begin in J^-(I+) and end in the black-hole region. [R1 F02 accepted; the earlier 'i.e. inside B' equivalence was false]
leaves.visibility.must_not_conflate[0]: bounded affine length is the notion used, not curvature-scalar blow-up; a curvature singularity inside a horizon is not a counterexample
leaves.visibility.must_not_conflate[1]: visibility is via a causal relation to a point of I+, not via a geodesic that merely escapes to spatial infinity i0
leaves.visibility.must_not_conflate[2]: a singularity hidden inside B is consistent with this class and is not a failure
leaves.visibility.must_not_conflate[3]: single-q non-containment (the formal negation) must not be replaced by B-containment; see negation_conclusion [R1 F02]

leaves.falsifier.tier_1.genericity_requirement: tier 1 refutes the class by showing the not-P set is NON-MEAGER in the ambient space (equivalently: it meets every comeager set). If the class is INSTANTIATED with a concrete, explicitly constructed generic set G*, then one datum in G* with not-P refutes the instantiated statement - a different, hypothesis-stronger claim. Route R1 = non-meagerness (general refutation); route R2 = a datum in an instantiated G* (instantiated claims only). [R1 F01 accepted; the earlier text wrongly made R1 a general route]

leaves.scope_statement: The maximal globally hyperbolic development of generic asymptotically flat vacuum initial data (4-dimensional Einstein vacuum equations, Lambda = 0) admits no proper future extension that is a C2 Lorentzian solution of the vacuum equations. The class is about non-extendibility of the development; it makes no statement about what an observer at I+ sees.
leaves.quantifiers.formal: forall r in D0: exists G_r subset X^r_vac(AF) with G_r comeager: forall (Sigma,h,K) in G_r, letting (M,g) be the maximal globally hyperbolic development: not exists a proper future C2 vacuum extension (M',g',iota) of (M,g).
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D0.definition: admissible regularity indices, a tagged disjoint union: r = smooth (the smooth-with-decay default) or r = (sobolev,s,delta) with s > 5/2 and delta in (1/2,1). X^r_vac(AF) is the corresponding one-ended AF vacuum constraint manifold (Frechet for r = smooth; weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1} for r = (sobolev,s,delta)). The index r ranges over exactly D0, so the smooth branch is no longer typed as a pair and the class does not range over 'suitable' regularity. [rev12 F-2 well-typedness repair: F1-review-19 F-2, F2b-review-034 HF-034-1]
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D1.definition: comeager (residual) subsets of X^r_vac(AF) in the named topology; X^r_vac(AF) minus G_r is meager
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D2.definition: one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum initial data satisfying both constraint equations in the declared regularity class
leaves.quantifiers.domains.D3.definition: proper future C2 vacuum extensions of the maximal development, in the exact sense of extension_predicate
leaves.quantifiers.order_note: the comeager set is fixed independently of the data; the extension quantifier is a negated existential over extensions of the given development, not over data

leaves.extension_predicate.name: proper_future_extension_in_class
leaves.extension_predicate.definition: A triple (M', g', iota) is a proper future C2 vacuum extension of (M,g) iff: (a) iota: M -> M' is an isometric embedding (iota_* g = g' restricted to iota(M)); (b) iota(M) is an open, proper subset of M'; (c) M' is connected and time-orientable, and its time orientation restricts to that of M; (d) g' is a C2 Lorentzian metric (signature (-,+,+,+), nondegenerate) on M'; (e) Ric(g') = 0 holds classically at every point of M' (g' of class C2 makes Ric continuous, so this is a pointwise statement); (f) the extension adds points to the future: there exist q in iota(M) and p in M' minus iota(M) with p in I^+(q; g').
leaves.extension_predicate.why_future_not_two_s: one-ended AF data can be extendible to the PAST into a white-hole region without any failure of future determinism; two-sided inextendibility is a strictly stronger different statement and is registered as a variant, not folded into this class.
leaves.extension_predicate.must_not_conflate[0]: a bare metric extension with no equation requirement is not a counterexample here; the extension must satisfy Ric(g') = 0
leaves.extension_predicate.must_not_conflate[1]: global hyperbolicity of M' is NOT required; requiring it would be a strictly weaker different statement
leaves.extension_predicate.must_not_conflate[2]: the maximal development is maximal among globally hyperbolic developments; that is not the same as inextendible among all solutions, which is what this class asserts
leaves.extension_predicate.must_not_conflate[3]: the extension is not required to contain Sigma as a Cauchy surface or to be maximal in any sense

leaves.genericity.ambient_space: the constraint manifold X^r_vac(AF) of one-ended asymptotically flat vacuum data, with the SUBSPACE topology induced from the weighted Sobolev product H^s_delta x H^{s-1}_{delta+1} (not the unconstrained product, under which X_vac would be meager and no G would exist). X_vac is a closed subset of a Banach space, hence Baire, so G is non-empty.
leaves.genericity.topology_or_measure: subspace topology on the constraint manifold; Frechet topology for the smooth-with-decay class. The diffeomorphism quotient is not used to define comeagerness (open technical gap).
leaves.genericity.generic_set: G = countable intersection of open dense subsets of X^r_vac(AF); complement meager; non-empty by Baire-ness
leaves.genericity.excluded_set: meager; must contain (status unresolved) the stationary/axisymmetric Kerr data, whose maximal development DOES admit a C-infinity vacuum extension, plus self-similar and finite-dimensional analytic families
leaves.genericity.class_change_warning: genericity is part of the class identity. The comeager form is this class. 'For all data' is strictly stronger. The dense-open form is ALSO strictly stronger, because a dense open set is comeager (it is the countable intersection of the constant family). The comeager form does not imply the dense-open form (a comeager set can have empty interior). No strengthening may be substituted silently.
leaves.genericity.transfer_failures[0].witness: let C = intersection over n of open dense U_n with measure < 1/n; C is comeager and null, so comeagerness does not yield full measure [R1 F03]
leaves.genericity.transfer_failures[1].witness: the complement of the comeager null set above is meager with full measure; the irrationals are both and witness nothing [R1 F03]
leaves.genericity.transfer_failures[2].witness: a fat Cantor set is meager with positive measure, hence not covered by countably many finite-codimension submanifolds
leaves.genericity.transfer_failures[3].witness: the irrationals are comeager with empty interior: a comeager set need not contain any nonempty open subset, so the comeager form does not yield a dense-open form
leaves.genericity.transfer_holds[0].witness: a dense open set U is the countable intersection of the constant family {U}, hence comeager; the dense-open form implies the comeager form
leaves.genericity.transfer_holds[1].witness: a proper closed finite-codimension submanifold is closed and nowhere dense, so a countable union of them is meager; if the exceptional set is so covered, the property holds on a comeager set
leaves.genericity.variants[1].relation: implied by residual_comeager in a Baire space (a comeager set is dense); a dense set need not be comeager, so it is strictly weaker than the class default. [R2-16 corrected: was off-vocabulary and mislabelled incomparable]

leaves.non_vacuity.condition: the class must be applied to data whose maximal development is not future geodesically complete. leaves.non_vacuity.status: trapped-surface formation is standard; membership of the family in G is UNVERIFIED here

leaves.non_vacuity.c2_specific_note: the vacuity argument (a future geodesically complete development admits no proper future extension) is ASSERTED here as a proof obligation, NOT as an established fact. The one-line reason (a maximal geodesic of the complete development cannot terminate at a boundary point of the extension) needs a Lorentzian-distance / causality step in M-prime, and M-prime is NOT assumed globally hyperbolic, so the step is not free. No counterexample is known in the frozen AF Lambda=0 class; the claim is marked UNVERIFIED pending a derivation or an L1 source. [R2 major accepted]

leaves.extension_predicate.definition: A triple (M', g', iota) is a proper future C0 metric extension of (M,g) iff: (a) iota: M -> M' is an isometric embedding (iota_* g = g' restricted to iota(M)); (b) iota(M) is an open, proper subset of M'; (c) M' is a SMOOTH (C-infinity) connected 4-manifold, time-orientable, whose time orientation restricts to that of M; the smooth structure is the category in which the metric is a tensor field, while the metric itself is only continuous (worker-16 F2b-16-03 accepted: a merely topological M' cannot carry a classical Lorentzian tensor field); (d) g' is a continuous, nondegenerate Lorentzian metric on M' (signature (-,+,+,+)); (e) NO equation is required of g' on M'; (f) the extension adds points to the future: int(M' minus iota(M)) is non-empty AND there exist q in iota(M) and p in int(M' minus iota(M)) with p in I^+(q; g'), where I^+ is the chronological future. The interior requirement blocks an extension that only adds boundary/dense-open points (R2 major: clause (f) was escapable). CONVENTION CAVEAT: for merely continuous metrics the causal structure can be degenerate and chronological futures may fail to be open or may depend on the curve class (Grant et al., worker-supplied pointer arXiv:1901.07996, UNVERIFIED); if the causal relation is degenerate, the witness must instead be a timelike curve from iota(M) to a point of int(M' minus iota(M)).
